notes.title: Published values, not a hardware readout
notes.text: No actuator has been queried. The per-joint values are defaults from a pinned Seeed configuration; actual firmware, saved registers and calibration may differ.

notes.title: MIT damping mismatch
notes.text: Joints 1–3 specify kd = 8 in Seeed’s YAML. Both the inspected MotorBridge encoder and Damiao V1.4 define kd = 0–5; that encoder clips 8 to 5. The installed MotorBridge version must be checked before assuming an effective gain.

notes.title: Mapping limits are not mechanical limits
notes.text: PMAX / VMAX / TMAX describe packet scaling. Joint travel, requested speeds, thermal ratings and modeled effort limits are separate quantities. The host and motor mapping scales must agree.

notes.title: Firmware-specific fields remain explicit
notes.text: The 53-register list is complete for the inspected MotorBridge table. It does not establish every register supported by every 4310 or 4340P firmware. Extended readbacks, raw scaling, reserved fields and undocumented coefficient behavior are marked accordingly.

notes.title: Different configuration layers
notes.text: Software YAML edits affect the host when loaded. Firmware RAM writes can be lost at power-off; storing parameters persists them. MIT command gains are sent in packets. This reference is read-only and does not apply any values to the simulator or hardware.

software.description: Host interface used to reach the actuators. The SDK selects the Damiao serial bridge for paths beginning /dev/tty.
Serial bridge rate fixed in the inspected SDK controller factory. This does not set the CAN wire bit rate.
Seeed’s SDK README gives a 500,000 bit/s SocketCAN example; the older Damiao V1.4 manual specifies 1,000,000 bit/s. Match the actual bridge and firmware; neither is a universal B601 setting.
Requested host control-loop frequency. It does not change the motor firmware’s internal servo frequency.
Default for RebotArmEndPose when no explicit mode is passed. It does not force every JointGroup into this mode; low-level groups initially track MIT.
Arm membership and command-array ordering; the six arm joints are controlled as one group.
Independent gripper group. Motor 7 drives the mechanism; the two simulated finger joints are a kinematic representation.
Logical key used to pair a software joint with its motor and group.
Chooses the actuator protocol implementation.
Selects the SDK’s initial position, velocity and torque mapping scales. A wrong model can mis-scale commands and feedback.
Software expectation for the receive ID; it does not itself prove or change the device’s ESC_ID.
Software expectation for the feedback arbitration ID, paired with MST_ID.
Position-error stiffness sent in MIT command packets. More stiffness produces more restoring torque for the same error.
Velocity-error damping sent in MIT packets. The inspected encoder clamps to 0–5; the first three YAML values are 8.
Written to RID 25 (KP_ASR) when the SDK configures position/velocity mode.
Written to RID 26 (KI_ASR) when configuring position/velocity mode.
Written to RID 27 (KP_APR); separate from the MIT proportional gain.
Written to RID 28 (KI_APR); actual loop semantics depend on firmware.
Velocity limit carried with each position/velocity target. This is an output command limit, separate from VMAX and rotor-side MAX_SPD.
Robot geometry, joint transforms, inertial properties and modeled limits used by host kinematics.
Frame whose position and orientation the host controller targets.
Compliant MIT stiffness while hand-guiding with gravity compensation. Whether YAML or constructor defaults apply depends on the caller.
Compliant damping used with gravity compensation.
Scales predicted gravity torque per arm joint to compensate for model-versus-hardware differences.
Time used to blend from stiff hold gains to compliant gains at startup.
Transforms joint signs for the model and maps gravity torques back to hardware. Not the same as firmware RID 55.
Stiff hold gains used before the compliant transition and when returning to a hold.
Restricts which named motors are enabled for that controller.
Diagnostic print interval; zero suppresses periodic output.
Loader can merge a named profile over the shared gravity settings; the inspected DM file defines no profiles.

commands.description: Target output position. The SDK send_mit call requires a position array; encoding uses 16 bits.
Desired velocity used by the damping term. Seeed defaults omitted velocity arrays to zero; encoding uses 12 bits.
Position-error gain in each command. A larger value raises restoring stiffness; this is separate from firmware KP_APR.
Velocity-error gain in each command. MotorBridge clamps outside values, including YAML kd = 8, to the encoding range.
Feedforward torque added to the position and velocity terms. Omitted arrays default to zero in the Seeed SDK.
Destination for the firmware position loop. This float format does not enforce the robot URDF travel limits by itself.
Travel-speed limit sent alongside each target position. ACC and DEC determine the non-MIT ramp.
Signed velocity request for the pure velocity mode. Direction follows the sign.
Position target used together with speed and torque/current limiting in supported mode-4 firmware.
Encoder clips the request to 0–100 and packs it at 0.01 resolution. This is a wire-format range, not the motor’s safe speed.
Normalized torque/current ceiling in supported mode 4. MotorBridge packs ratio × 10,000; this is not a torque value in N·m.

modes.name: MIT
modes.description: Combines position, velocity, stiffness, damping and feedforward torque in one packed command.

modes.name: Position / velocity
modes.description: Firmware moves toward a position with a commanded speed limit and its own motion ramp.

modes.name: Velocity
modes.description: Firmware tracks a signed velocity request.

modes.name: Force / position
modes.description: Position command with speed and torque/current limits. Listed by MotorBridge; the older V1.4 manual covers only modes 1–3.

operations.name: Enable
operations.description: Allows the drive to produce torque and accept motion commands.

operations.name: Disable
operations.description: Turns off active drive torque; this is not a mechanical brake.

operations.name: Save position zero
operations.description: Makes the present mechanical pose the encoder zero reference. This changes the relationship between commands and arm geometry.

operations.name: Clear error
operations.description: Clears a latched error; the underlying fault can remain and trigger again.

operations.name: Read register
operations.description: Retrieves a firmware value without changing it. Use readback to establish actual device configuration.

operations.name: Write register
operations.description: Changes a writable value. The driver distinguishes a RAM write from saving parameters.

operations.name: Store parameters
operations.description: Commits changed configuration to nonvolatile storage so it survives power cycling. The manufacturer GUI’s “write parameters” action can reset the controller.

operations.name: Request feedback
operations.description: Requests or refreshes position, velocity, torque, temperature and status feedback.

operations.name: Sensor calibration / parameter identification
operations.description: Manufacturer commissioning routines identify encoder alignment and motor properties. These are not ordinary gain controls.

operations.name: Firmware version / firmware update
operations.description: Version readback identifies the drive implementation; firmware replacement can change register support and behavior.

registers.name: UV_Value
registers.description: Supply threshold below which the driver protects itself from undervoltage.

registers.name: KT_Value
registers.description: Torque-to-current coefficient, called KT_OUT in the manual. Zero selects the firmware’s calculated coefficient in V1.4.

registers.name: OT_Value
registers.description: Motor winding temperature trip threshold. Raising it permits a hotter motor before shutdown.

registers.name: OC_Value
registers.description: Fraction of the peak phase-current limit. 0.5 means 50%; this is not a value in amperes.

registers.name: ACC
registers.description: Acceleration ramp used outside MIT mode. Confirm the scaling in the installed firmware before interpreting a raw value.

registers.name: DEC
registers.description: Deceleration ramp outside MIT mode. The register table uses a negative value; compare magnitudes with ACC.

registers.name: MAX_SPD
registers.description: Rotor-side speed ceiling for velocity mode in V1.4. This differs from the command vlim and the VMAX mapping scale.

registers.name: MST_ID
registers.description: CAN arbitration ID used for feedback. The B601-DM software expects 0x11–0x17.

registers.name: ESC_ID
registers.description: Base CAN receive ID for an actuator. The B601-DM software assigns 0x01–0x07; mode-dependent command offsets are added.

registers.name: TIMEOUT
registers.description: Watchdog count before loss-of-command protection. Example: 20,000 ticks = 1 second. Zero behavior is not specified here.

registers.name: CTRL_MODE
registers.description: Selects the command format: 1 MIT, 2 position/velocity, 3 velocity, 4 force/position in MotorBridge. Mode 4 depends on firmware support.

registers.name: Damp
registers.description: Identified viscous damping. The V1.4 manual describes it as a reference value unused by that firmware; it is not MIT kd.

registers.name: Inertia
registers.description: Identified rotor inertia. A motor-model property, separate from payload inertia or the robot URDF.

registers.name: hw_ver
registers.description: Named hardware version, but reserved in the inspected table. No portable interpretation is documented.

registers.name: sw_ver
registers.description: Firmware software-version identifier. Record it when comparing register behavior across actuators.

registers.name: SN
registers.description: Named serial number, but reserved in the inspected table. Do not assume a usable unique serial.

registers.name: NPP
registers.description: Number of magnetic pole pairs used by commutation. MotorBridge exposes this as read-only.

registers.name: Rs
registers.description: Identified phase resistance. Confirm raw-register scaling against the specific firmware; the old UI lists milliohms.

registers.name: Ls
registers.description: Identified phase inductance. Confirm raw-register scaling against firmware; the old UI lists microhenries. Also spelled LS in other libraries.

registers.name: Flux
registers.description: Identified magnetic flux linkage used by the motor model.

registers.name: Gr
registers.description: Gear reduction ratio, used to relate rotor movement to output-shaft movement. Read-only in this CAN register table.

registers.name: PMAX
registers.description: Positive magnitude used to map position to and from the packed CAN representation (−PMAX to +PMAX). It is not a joint travel limit.

registers.name: VMAX
registers.description: Positive magnitude used to encode and decode velocity (−VMAX to +VMAX). It is not the requested operating speed.

registers.name: TMAX
registers.description: Positive magnitude used to encode and decode torque (−TMAX to +TMAX). It is not a continuous-duty torque rating.

registers.name: I_BW
registers.description: Current-loop bandwidth setting. Faster response changes noise sensitivity and stability. The inspected table does not state a physical unit.

registers.name: KP_ASR
registers.description: Velocity-loop proportional gain: response to present speed error. Written from POS_VEL.vel_kp by Seeed’s SDK.

registers.name: KI_ASR
registers.description: Velocity-loop integral gain: accumulates speed error to reduce steady error. Written from POS_VEL.vel_ki.

registers.name: KP_APR
registers.description: Position-loop proportional gain in position/velocity control. Written from POS_VEL.pos_kp; separate from MIT kp.

registers.name: KI_APR
registers.description: Position-loop integral gain in the register table, written from POS_VEL.pos_ki. V1.4’s appendix calls this a speed integral term, so its exact firmware behavior needs confirmation.

registers.name: OV_Value
registers.description: Upper supply-voltage threshold. The old V1.4 manual describes checking it at power-up; continuous checking is not established for every firmware.

registers.name: GREF
registers.description: Gearbox torque transmission efficiency used by torque conversion. It is a motor-model correction factor.

registers.name: Deta
registers.description: Speed-loop damping factor. Smaller values may increase overshoot; larger values may slow the response. Separate from MIT kd.

registers.name: V_BW
registers.description: Filtering bandwidth for the velocity loop. Sets the response/noise tradeoff; the inspected sources do not establish a universal unit.

registers.name: IQ_c1
registers.description: Current-loop enhancement coefficient. The driver names it but does not document its internal equation or tuning method.

registers.name: VL_c1
registers.description: Velocity-loop enhancement coefficient. Internal implementation and tuning effects are not specified in the inspected sources.

registers.name: can_br
registers.description: Selects the CAN bit-rate code on supporting firmware. Code-to-bit-rate mapping is not established by these sources; do not infer it from serial baud.

registers.name: sub_ver
registers.description: Firmware sub-version identifier, useful alongside sw_ver.

registers.name: u_off
registers.description: U-phase calibration offset. Driver metadata does not define its raw unit or correction equation.

registers.name: v_off
registers.description: V-phase calibration offset. Driver metadata does not define its raw unit or correction equation.

registers.name: k1
registers.description: First internal compensation coefficient. Its exact role is not described in the public register table.

registers.name: k2
registers.description: Second internal compensation coefficient. Its exact role is not described in the public register table.

registers.name: m_off
registers.description: Angle offset labeled m_off. The inspected table does not identify its reference frame or scale.

registers.name: dir
registers.description: Direction/calibration flag. The table declares a float but does not specify allowed values; do not assume it is a ±1 software direction setting.

registers.name: m_off
registers.description: Motor-side angle offset, also named m_off in MotorBridge. Use RID 56 to distinguish it from RID 54; availability depends on firmware.

registers.name: Imax
registers.description: Reported maximum current of the driver board. This is read-only capability data, distinct from OC_Value.

registers.name: VBus
registers.description: Supply-bus voltage readback. The register table does not define its raw scaling.

registers.name: Tpcb
registers.description: Driver-board temperature readback. Confirm scaling before treating the raw value as degrees Celsius.

registers.name: Tmtr
registers.description: Motor temperature readback. Confirm scaling; the standard feedback frame separately reports winding temperature in °C.

registers.name: Iu_off
registers.description: U-phase current-sensor calibration offset; firmware-dependent readback.

registers.name: Iv_off
registers.description: V-phase current-sensor calibration offset; firmware-dependent readback.

registers.name: Iw_off
registers.description: W-phase current-sensor calibration offset; firmware-dependent readback.

registers.name: p_m
registers.description: Motor position readback. The register table does not fully establish its coordinate convention or units.

registers.name: xout
registers.description: Output-shaft position readback. Distinguish this from motor-side position; verify zero and scaling on the specific firmware.
